how: Members call for help drawing Ryu at a specified location and separately invite help making Chun-Li.
Members accept invitations through a brief placing report or an unqualified promise to contribute.
Calls receive explicit bare joins, supporting the acceptance mechanism without testing refusals or silent participation.
Members describe crowded space and weigh gathering many more people against asking territorial maintainers.
The first caller also reports building a leg, and another member reports joining the attempt.
The initial turn combines starting the character and calling helpers rather than separating them into independently evidenced causal stages.
Builders report work on a leg and the placement of one white dot without establishing a finished mark.
The invitation receives a report that a helper placed a white dot.
Members propose an easier Ryu and refine its palette to fit the available colors.
Anchor coordinates locate alternative designs without establishing an agreed pixel-by-pixel template.
Design feasibility includes adapting colors and reusing an existing motif rather than only choosing a representative character.
Design proposals include coordinates before any evidenced agreement, so a template settling collective design remains unobserved.
Contribution reports establish participation but cannot establish whether organizational order was decided elsewhere.
Immediate pixel replacement does not reveal scripts, bots, spare accounts, or their use by this room.
Participants attribute replacement to territorial maintainers while the initial erasure diagnosis remains explicitly tentative.
Immediate displacement establishes a lost placement but does not establish organized repair or defence.
Progressing from building to upkeep requires a retainable placement, whereas an initial dot can be immediately displaced before organized repair is evidenced.
A replacement report establishes neither organized upkeep nor machine escalation, leaving the proposed upkeep-to-automation mechanism untestable.
Members treat a territorial maintainer's approval as a prerequisite for keeping the proposed character in its area.
Internal advice to seek a host's permission precedes any evidenced request, host ruling, or authorized guest artwork.
The asking-for-space placement applies here only to advice to ask, because delivery of a request is not established.
Internal suggestions to contact maintainers do not establish negotiation with a neighbour.
Proposed contact and reported thanks do not establish an envoy carrying a proposal between communities.
Mentioning Discord as a possible contact route does not establish coalition membership or shared organizing.
Advice to seek territorial approval does not establish sparing, apology, restraint, or an appeal delivered to attackers.
Recognizing territorial approval as necessary does not establish a dispute over who may commit either room.
Neither an agreement nor a challenge to its representative is established, so the tentative agreement-to-authority-dispute mechanism cannot be tested.
A proposed easier design at another location must remain distinguishable from an implemented relocation after confirmed loss.
A manpower deficit leaves asking maintainers as an explicit alternative, so moving requires an additional choice to abandon the occupied target.
A member reports thanking another group for a character it is making, without establishing alliance membership or reciprocal pixel aid.
Advice to contact maintainers does not establish a transition from organized upkeep to actual border negotiation.
A settled border and subsequent restraint are not established by advice that permission is needed.
Thanks for another group's character do not establish upkeep strain causing a request for and receipt of outside help.
The reported thanks establish neither prior border negotiation nor a subsequent exchange of help.
Proposed contact through chat establishes neither organized upkeep nor coalition formation.
The easier-design proposal names an existing character to replace without identifying a quarrel predating the canvas.
Character selection and functional reuse do not establish ideological allegiance, inherited quarrels, or collective identity beyond representation.
The replacement proposal gives ease and an existing motif as reasons without naming a prior tie that makes the builders rivals.
Participants test apparent April Fools reveals through cost, timing, provisional outside reports, clarification, and live evidence.
Members react to the room's banner scare with predictions, laughter, approval, and a wish to retain it.
Recipients actively test whether a reveal is genuine, a practice distinct from staging the deception themselves.
Retention requires an experienced change to preserve, whereas hoping an apparent joke becomes a playable release remains prospective.
Explains hoping fan response produces a playable release and judging the emotional cost and missing practical features of an apparent joke.
The banner reaction and canvas invitations do not establish a canvas megathread, removal policy, flood complaint, or dedicated organizing sub.
Character invitations do not establish a flood of canvas posts or a host boundary response to one.
A participant tentatively reports erasure in answer to a location question during the attempt.
Recording fate includes provisional live diagnosis before any evidenced completion or collective celebration.
A location question elicits a tentative loss report during construction, providing an entry into fate-recording without evidenced celebration.
A single-pixel report and appreciation of another group's character do not establish completion celebration or collective credit for this room's mark.
The wish to retain a separate April Fools banner does not establish carrying canvas work or its organization onward.
A tentative live erasure diagnosis supplies no evidence of post-placement disputes over cleanup, historical damage, or corrected accounts.
An initial placing report does not establish completion followed by collective celebration.
The tentative fate report is evidenced, but a preceding celebration that generates recording is not.
The tentative live fate report does not establish later preservation or continuation generated by that record.
A member calls for replacing existing character art to make the easier design, without establishing execution or a hostile rivalry.
The replacement proposal follows recruitment as a design simplification, so a hostile mobilization mechanism requires evidence beyond the ordering of these turns.
The replacement proposal contains no evidenced exchange of taunts, victory claims, or rival-directed spoken contest.
The replacement proposal does not establish a later refusal, apology, or restraint response.
A replacement proposal and internal contact advice do not establish an attack generating actual negotiation with neighbours.
The replacement proposal does not establish a subsequent spoken contest with its target.
